name: Ananias the high priest
charge: Commanding Paul to be smitten on the mouth, contrary to the law, while sitting to judge him by the law
summary: Paul had said one sentence to the council when the high priest ordered him struck. Paul answered as a prophet answers: God shall smite thee, thou whited wall; for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law? Then he withdrew the words toward the office, not the man.
offense: Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day. And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth. The law forbids condemning a man before he is heard, and forbids the judge to strike the accused; Ananias did both from the judgment seat.
judgment: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall. Told it was the high priest, he answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people. Scripture records the word spoken and not its performance; the office was honoured, the man was named, and the sentence was left with God.

entries.commentary: If there be a controversy between men, the judges justify the righteous and condemn the wicked; the wicked man worthy to be beaten was made to lie down and be beaten before the judge's face, according to his fault, by a certain number. Forty stripes may he give him, and not exceed, lest thy brother should seem vile unto thee. Paul recounted receiving that beating under this law.

Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn: the corn is the reward for the ox. Paul applies this verse to how the elders are treated: let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine, for the labourer is worthy of his reward. Giving double honour is not just saying the words to the leadership; it is true respect and reverence toward the leadership that labours in this word and doctrine.

If brethren dwell together and one of them die and have no child, the wife of the dead was not to marry without unto a stranger; her husband's brother took her to wife, and the firstborn she bare succeeded in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. Check this out: this is no longer the law, so do not try to use it as an excuse toward your brother's wife. It stood for the name not being put out because of the land inheritance in Israel. The man who refused was called before the elders; his brother's wife loosed his shoe from off his foot, spat in his face, and answered, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother's house; and his name was called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.

Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt: he met thee by the way and smote the hindmost of thee, all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary, and he feared not God. Israel was later commanded through Samuel to repay it: I remember that which Amalek did to Israel; now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not. At Rephidim, where Amalek first came and fought with Israel, the Lord told Moses to write this for a memorial in a book and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua, for the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation; and that war is still going on even to this day.

If a man steal an ox or a sheep and kill it or sell it, he restores five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep. We are in a different situation where we do not keep oxen and sheep, but the principle of restitution still applies among brothers and sisters in the body: if something is stolen, the law written here governs the payback. Do not be stealing.

If a thief be found breaking up means breaking in. He entered your home and you defended yourself and he died: that is what is called self-defense today, and no blood is shed for him, meaning there is no judgment. The judgment was already passed in the breaking in. If the sun be risen upon him, the thief got away, and there shall be blood shed for him means there shall be a judgment; then the verse gives the judgment. He makes full restitution, and if he have nothing he is sold for his theft: not sold into slavery, but into work servitude until he pays off the debt of what he stole. If the theft be found in his hand alive, he restores double. Verse three covers the thief who already got rid of what he stole; verse four covers the one still holding it.

These are self-explanatory: if a man lets his beast feed in another man's field or vineyard, he makes restitution of the best of his own field and vineyard; and he that kindles a fire that consumes another man's corn surely makes restitution.

If a man deliver money or stuff to his neighbor to keep and it be stolen, the thief found pays double. If the thief be not found, the master of the house is brought unto the judges, to see whether he put his hand unto his neighbor's goods, whether he was part of a scheme to deceive the owner out of his goods. For all manner of trespass, whether for ox, ass, sheep, raiment, or any lost thing, both parties come before the judges, and whom the judges condemn pays double unto his neighbor.

If a beast delivered to a neighbor to keep die or be hurt or driven away, no man seeing it, an oath of the Lord is between them both. In layman's terms he swears: I did not take the stuff, I did not set you up, I do not know where it is. The owner accepts the oath and the matter ends there; it is not to be spoken of again. Paul uses this civil law to show how the Most High is unchangeable. An oath for confirmation is the end of all strife; God confirmed his counsel by an oath, and by two immutable things, that it is impossible for God to lie and that he will not take back what went out of his mouth, we have strong consolation. The same way, once the oath of this law is applied, the matter is over.

If the thing kept be stolen from him, he makes restitution; if it be torn in pieces, he brings it for witness and does not make it good. If a man borrow ought of his neighbor, ought meaning anything, and it be hurt or die with the owner not present, he surely makes it good. You borrowed it, it got messed up, you owe the man. But if the owner be with it, or if it be an hired thing, it came for its hire. If you came to plow a man's field for ten shekels with your own donkey and your donkey breaks his leg, you cannot expect the owner to pay for your own faulty equipment; the same as a business loan today, the property owner is not liable when your own equipment breaks down.

If a man entice a maid that is not betrothed and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife; he has to sign the papers. He is at fault for not going through the proper channels of marriage, and she is at fault for being enticed and laying down. The proper channel was that the father married off the daughter. To marry thy daughter is to perform a weighty matter, for the father gives her over to that man for the rest of her life and is out of all watching over her; so she is to be given to a man of understanding, one keeping the commandments as a wise man. In our own land the daughter went from her father's house to a husband's house with the blessing of the father.

Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live: witchcraft goes into horoscopes, palm readings, and all things of that nature. Whosoever lieth with a beast, bestiality, shall surely be put to death. He that sacrificeth unto any god save unto the Lord only shall be utterly destroyed.

This is twofold, and first and foremost the stranger is your brother from a different area, our own people. [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25) shows it: if thy brother be waxen poor, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, sojourn meaning travel, thou shalt relieve him that he may live with thee. A brother of another tribe who falls on hard times and travels down to live with you is that stranger; neither vex him nor oppress him, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.

Ye shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child. A wife without a husband already has a hard life, and a son or daughter without a father the same; do not make their life harder than it already is. If thou afflict them in any wise and they cry unto the Most High, he will surely hear their cry, and his wrath shall wax hot: he will kill you with the sword, and your own wives shall be widows and your children fatherless. That is the Lord's plain warning against mistreating those less fortunate.

Usury means interest. You cannot charge your brother or sister interest: if you lend twenty dollars, you get twenty dollars back, nothing more, nothing less; no little bit more off the top. This is the same law read in [Leviticus 25:36-37](/bible/leviticus/25#v36).

If thou take thy neighbor's raiment to pledge, deliver it unto him by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only; wherein shall he sleep? The tunics and overcoats worn then were also sleeping garments to keep a man warm at night, especially the poor. A well-off man does not have to work for you; this speaks of the less fortunate who extend their services for money and give what is most valuable to them, their raiment, as the pledge. If he cries unto the Most High, he will hear, for he is gracious.

Thou shalt not revile the gods means do not hate or speak evil of your leaders. The word gods here is the leaders over you: the Most High says in the psalm, I have said, Ye are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High, speaking of us. [Acts 23](/bible/acts/23) is the example: when Paul spoke against the high priest, they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest? And Paul answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people, quoting this very verse.

Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits and of thy liquors, and the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give unto me. The firstborn sons that opened the matrix were consecrated unto the Lord, and the father redeemed them back from the priest with shekels. Likewise with the oxen and the sheep: seven days the firstling stayed with his dam, his mother, and on the eighth day it was given. The Lord did not want it too young, taken as soon as it popped out; it had to be its appointed time with the mother, then brought to the priest.

Ye shall be holy men unto me: neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs. This is twofold, and the dogs are the strangers of other nations, the aliens and foreigners. Always get the context of the law, because sometimes the stranger is your brother and sometimes it is literally the other nations. [Deuteronomy 14:21](/bible/deuteronomy/14#v21) doubles this law: that which dieth of itself thou shalt give unto the stranger that is in thy gates, or sell it unto an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God. Cast the torn flesh to the other nations; ye shall not eat it, because ye are holy people.

The word of the Lord came telling Ezekiel to prophesy against the prophets of Israel that prophesy out of their own hearts. Woe unto the foolish prophets that follow their own spirit and have seen nothing, just like the pastors today who follow the spirit of the white man, the spirit of Esau, Christmas, and all these things, changing our people and giving them a false sense of security that they will get the kingdom of heaven. The prophets are like the foxes in the desert, using craftiness in a ruined and wasted area of Israel to make gain among the people, the same as a well-groomed church in a run-down area of the hood where the pastor makes gain off the people. They have not gone up into the gaps nor made up the hedge for the house of Israel to stand in the battle in the day of the Lord, meaning they did not protect Israel from the Lord's wrath the way Moses stood in the gap when we went into idolatry. They have seen vanity and lying divination, saying the Lord sent them when He had not, making Israel hope their lies would be confirmed.

Because they speak vanity and see lies, the Most High is against them; His hand will be upon the prophets that see vanity and divine lies. They shall not be in the assembly of His people, nor written in the writing of the house of Israel, nor enter the land of Israel, meaning they will die in captivity. They have seduced His people with another spirit, saying peace when there is no peace, the way pastors today seduce our people with the spirit of white jesus and not the spirit of the Most High of this Bible. One built a wall and others daubed it with untempered mortar, patchwork upon the wall of Jerusalem, the prophets saying peace and safety while telling the people to build the walls up.

The Most High will rend the wall with a stormy wind in His fury, with an overflowing shower in His anger and great hailstones in His fury to consume it. He will break down the wall daubed with untempered mortar and bring it to the ground so its foundation is discovered, and they shall be consumed in the midst of it and know He is the Lord. He will accomplish His wrath upon the wall and upon them that daubed it, the prophets of Israel which prophesied concerning Jerusalem and saw visions of peace for her when there was no peace, because of our sins.

Ezekiel is to set his face against the daughters of his people which prophesy out of their own heart, just like the female pastors today who want to prophesy and teach our people and teach the men. Woe to the women that sew pillows to all armholes and make kerchiefs upon the head of every stature to hunt souls; the pillows are the wide robe-like openings down the arm and the kerchief is the covering placed on the head. They hunt the souls of the Most High's people and pollute His word among the people, saying God loves everybody and praise white jesus, doing it back then for handfuls of barley and pieces of bread and today for money.

The Most High is against their pillows, wherewith they hunt the souls to make them fly, meaning to fly into sin and wickedness; He will tear them from their arms and let the hunted souls go free. He will use men who keep His commandments to go out and teach the people the proper way and tear them from the arms of these wicked women. He will tear their kerchiefs and deliver His people out of their hand, so they shall be no more in their hand to be hunted, and they shall know He is the Lord.

With lies they made the heart of the righteous sad whom the Most High had not made sad, and strengthened the hands of the wicked that he should not return from his wicked way by promising him life. That is what happens today: the righteous are made sad by these women carrying on with no Bible in hand, just talking lies, while they strengthen the hands of the wicked and the people that put them in power. Therefore they shall see no more vanity nor divine divinations, for the Most High will deliver His people out of their hand, and they shall know He is the Lord.

verses.text: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.
And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?
And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest?
Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.
If there be a controversy between men, and they come unto judgment, that the judges may judge them; then they shall justify the righteous, and condemn the wicked.
And it shall be, if the wicked man be worthy to be beaten, that the judge shall cause him to lie down, and to be beaten before his face, according to his fault, by a certain number.
Doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth?
Thou shalt not revile the gods, nor curse the ruler of thy people.
Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace; and one built up a wall, and, lo, others daubed it with untempered morter:
Say unto them which daub it with untempered morter, that it shall fall: there shall be an overflowing shower; and ye, O great hailstones, shall fall; and a stormy wind shall rend it.
Lo, when the wall is fallen, shall it not be said unto you, Where is the daubing wherewith ye have daubed it?
Therefore thus saith the Lord God; I will even rend it with a stormy wind in my fury; and there shall be an overflowing shower in mine anger, and great hailstones in my fury to consume it.

So will I break down the wall that ye have daubed with untempered morter, and bring it down to the ground, so that the foundation thereof shall be discovered, and it shall fall, and ye shall be consumed in the midst thereof: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.
Thus will I accomplish my wrath upon the wall, and upon them that have daubed it with untempered morter, and will say unto you, The wall is no more, neither they that daubed it;
